articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Giants trade for McCarthy, Bucs lose Mayfield for three weeks
articles.description: How do QB moves in New York and Tampa Bay affect the Giants' and Bucaneers' receivers?
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 28: QB-depleted Giants trade for J.J. McCarthy

By Eric Karabell

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, not too long ago the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, is now a member of the New York Giants, after they sent a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for his services. In some ways, this is stunning. The Vikings gave up on McCarthy after one terrible season in which he completed only 57.6% of his passes and accrued more interceptions than touchdown passes. He is 23, but the Vikings may or may not be set with their future quarterback, depending on how newcomer Kyler Murray performs. Early returns -- for Murray's performance and durability -- are quite mixed.

The Giants are taking a chance on an intriguing prospect, even if McCarthy did not play well during his first active season. Then again, the Giants already have an intriguing quarterback prospect in Jaxson Dart, the No. 25 pick in the 2025 draft. Dart remains the future quarterback here, but concussions marred his rookie campaign, and this season ended in Week 2 with major tears in his left knee. Nobody knows if Dart can stay healthy for the entirety of a full season, which is why this trade makes sense for the Giants.

For fantasy purposes, those who roster Dart in a keeper/dynasty league should already have been quite worried about his future in terms of staying on the field. This trade doesn't necessarily alter that. McCarthy missed his entire rookie season of 2024 with a knee injury, too. The Giants add another body who, when healthy, needs to prove himself on the field. Dart has done that part already.

As for this season's Giants, veteran backup Jameis Winston seems likely to remain the starting quarterback for as long as he is healthy and competent. He was competent enough Sunday, leading the team to a 12-7 win over the Titans, even though he did little to aid fantasy managers statistically. Winston threw for only 118 yards, albeit in difficult weather conditions, but he avoided turnovers. The Winston who passed for 5,109 yards, 33 touchdowns and 30 interceptions for the 2019 Buccaneers is long gone, not returning.

Expect Winston to remain the starter, and assuming the Giants prefer Winston to act cautiously as a passer, merely directing the offense and attempting safe throws, it already impedes the upside for WRs Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields, and TE Isaiah Likely. articles.headline: Sources: Panthers CB Jaycee Horn out indefinitely with torn quad
articles.description: Panthers cornerback Jaycee Horn will seek a second opinion on his torn quad, sources told NFL Network, but he is headed for injured reserve and could miss the rest of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers cornerback Jaycee Horn sustained a torn quad during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Cleveland Browns, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Horn will seek a second opinion, sources said, but he is headed for injured reserve and could miss the rest of the 2026 season. Sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler that Horn could miss six to 12 weeks.

Horn was injured on the game-winning touchdown throw by Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson to tight end Harold Fannin Jr. with 1:48 to play. Horn was seen on the ground in the end zone near the Browns' sideline following the play. He was checked out by trainers, who then assisted Horn off the field.

"We're going to have to evaluate that and see where he's at," coach Dave Canales said of Horn after Sunday's loss. "But he was not going to be coming back in."

The injury news was better for wide receiver Jalen Coker. A source told Rapoport that Coker suffered a minor quad strain against the Browns and will be considered questionable for "Sunday Night Football" against the Detroit Lions.

Coker, who also had been dealing with an ankle injury, played throughout the first half before ultimately leaving the game. He has 18 receptions for 222 yards and two touchdowns this season.

Starting cornerback Mike Jackson injured his groin in the first half and was replaced by special teams ace Akayleb Evans throughout the second half. Horn was replaced by rookie Will Lee, the team's third cornerback in the positional pecking order, after he was helped off the field.

The Panthers also have longtime nickel cornerback Chau Smith-Wade on the roster. Corey Thornton, who played quite a bit last season, is on the practice squad.

Carolina also played Sunday without linebacker Devin Lloyd, who had been ruled out with a calf injury a week after recording two interceptions and scoring a touchdown during a win over the Atlanta Falcons.

The Panthers have a bye in Week 5.

The other 28 teams in the association will join them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams Tuesday.

Sept. 28

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks

New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason, and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' annual media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at Madison Square Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperation with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent Jr.'s deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant

Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's Media Day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. ...I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's Media Day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. ... Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

articles.headline: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter through 2026 season
articles.description: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. However, unlike his rookie season, the plan was for the 2025 No. 2 overall pick to be a starter on defense. Now, he is just being mixed in on offense with a specific package of plays. The situation is fluid, though, and head coach Liam Coen has maintained that Hunter's usage could change weekly.

"You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches [on offense], then [he] absolutely will."

Hunter played more on offense than defense in his 2025 rookie season, which ended after seven games because of a right knee injury. The 2024 Heisman Trophy winner had 28 catches for 298 yards and a touchdown and 15 tackles and three pass breakups. He played 67% of the team's offensive snaps and 36% of the defensive snaps before his injury, which occurred during practice on Oct. 30.

How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

Week 3 vs. New England Patriots

In a 35-6 win against the Patriots, Hunter saw an increase in snaps with 42 on defense (70%) and a decrease on offense with four snaps (6.7% of all offensive snaps). He recorded four tackles and his first career interception, picking off New England quarterback Drake Maye in the back of the end zone late in the first half to preserve the Jaguars' 14-3 lead. Maye was trying to hit receiver Efton Chism III on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, but Hunter out-jumped Chism for the ball. Hunter didn't touch the ball on offense for the second consecutive game, leaving him with only two touches so far this season.

Week 2 at Denver Broncos

Hunter played 43 total snaps in the loss against the Broncos: 35 on defense (59.3% of all defensive snaps), seven on offense (12.7% of all offensive snaps) and one on special teams. He had one pass breakup and four tackles, and he was penalized for pass interference on a Bo Nix sideline pass to receiver Courtland Sutton. The 22-yard penalty -- plus Coen's unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing the call -- gave the Broncos the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line. The Broncos scored what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown on the next play. Hunter was not targeted on offense.

After Week 2, Coen explained that his cornerbacks are handling drives with a planned rotation -- which is why Hunter was in for only 59.3% of defensive plays.

"We did it for the most part of the last season as well, before Travis got hurt," Coen said. "It's something that we got to continue to do. We have corners that we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us. They've been in the system now.

articles.headline: LeBron James says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent
articles.description: LeBron James told ESPN that he envisioned joining the Knicks as a free agent this summer, but nixed the idea after New York won the NBA title.
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- LeBron James said his free agency decision came down to five teams: the Philadelphia 76ers, Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Miami Heat and Minnesota Timberwolves.

But there was another team James had planned to join -- before that franchise ended a 53-year championship drought in June: the New York Knicks.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' annual media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James said that the potential backlash from joining the Knicks after they had won the title rendered the idea a non-starter.

"Y'all wouldn't have let me lay that down, at all," James said, referring to the media at large. "But much respect to the Knicks, obviously. An unbelievable team, unbelievable players. Shout out Jalen Brunson. I love that guy, he's unbelievable. But, yeah, I'm happy where I'm at and I'm looking forward to it."

The Knicks swept the Sixers in the second round in May, winning by an average of 22.3 points per game.

James will get two chances to play in the Garden during the regular season: Opening Night on Oct. 20 and on Feb. 27 -- plus potentially more if there is a postseason rematch.

And he will still get time in New York, even though he's playing for the Sixers.

James told ESPN that he will split his time living between the Big Apple and the City of Brotherly Love.

"Both," he said. "Multiple residences."

articles.headline: Buccaneers' Mayfield (thumb) out at least three weeks, Bowles says
articles.description: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is expected to miss at least three weeks with the dislocated thumb on his throwing hand he suffered Sunday, coach Todd Bowles announced Monday.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is expected to miss at least three weeks with the dislocated thumb on his throwing hand he suffered Sunday, coach Todd Bowles announced Monday.

Mayfield's MRI showed no additional damage to his right thumb, sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Jenna Laine.

Mayfield, however, still needs to be able to grip the ball, a source told Laine, but he avoided damage to the ligament or tendon.

Rookie Jalon Daniels will replace the injured Mayfield as the Buccaneers' starting quarterback.

Mayfield's injury occurred with 1:54 remaining, when his pass was intercepted by Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel. The play happened on fourth-and-13, with Mayfield and the Bucs trying to come back from a 20-16 deficit. He was under duress for several seconds and evaded multiple defenders as he scurried to the right sideline. But as he threw the ball, he was hit by inside linebacker Blake Cashman.

Mayfield's 54 regular-season starts since joining the Buccaneers are tied for most in the league. He has never missed a start in Tampa Bay despite an injury-marred season last year that saw him on the injury report for 10 out of 17 weeks.

articles.headline: Giannis confident in what he can offer to overhauled Heat
articles.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo has no doubt about his potential as he enters the next stage of his career following a blockbuster trade to the Heat, saying he can still "dominate the game" as one of the best players in the world.
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo has no doubt about his potential as he enters the next stage of his career following a blockbuster trade to the Miami Heat.

"I really do believe that, if not the best, I'm one of the best players in the world," Antetokounmpo said Monday at Heat media day. "I know when I'm at my best, when I'm locked in, when my body is right, I really do believe that I can dominate the game and I can impact the game in both ways, offensively and defensively. I think I've shown it over the years."

The two-time MVP who led the Milwaukee Bucks to an NBA title in 2021 officially starts the next chapter of his career Tuesday, when the Heat open training camp in Boca Raton, Florida. He was the centerpiece of a massive roster restructuring by Miami this summer, one that saw the Heat add Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis and Tim Hardaway Jr., among others, to a core led by Bam Adebayo, Andrew Wiggins, Pelle Larsson and Davion Mitchell.

"This is all new for me," Antetokounmpo said. "I'm trying to learn defense. I'm learning offenses. I am trying to fit in the locker room with new faces. I'm trying to be able to play with players that I've never played before. It's all new for me. It's exciting.

"I know that I'm going to put in the work. Succeed or fail, I'm going to fail by working or succeed by working. And the goal is to win a championship. That's the goal."

The Kaseya Center, the Heat's home arena, is a construction site these days. Dozens of workers in hard hats, orange reflective vests and steel-toed boots are all over the building, putting the finishing touches on new club spaces and other amenities that will greet fans in a couple of weeks.

Seems fitting that the team has gone through a refurbishment of sorts as well.

"I feel like there's a synergy from a lot of people in the building about this opportunity and the appropriate time," Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said. "Some things in this league really are about alignment. And then we'll see how it all plays out once we get into the competition and the games and all that."

Antetokounmpo entered the NBA in 2013. His career totals to date: 21,531 points, 8,882 rebounds and 4,484 assists. The point and rebound totals are both fifth best in the NBA over that span, while the assist total is 13th best.

Those numbers are just part of the reason why the Heat consider him to still be one of the five best players in the NBA.

"We brought him here for a reason. He's here for a reason," Spoelstra said. "We want him to establish himself as in that conversation of being the best player in the league, and that can be debated in a lot of different ways. But we're not bringing him here to take a step back, so we'll try to maximize his strengths as much as we can and get him as comfortable as possible."

articles.headline: Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis out with 'health issue'
articles.description: Kristaps Porzingis will miss the start of Warriors training camp because of a health issue.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- The Golden State Warriors will be without starting center Kristaps Porzingis to open training camp because of a "health issue," general manager Mike Dunleavy announced Monday.

The Warriors are keeping the details private and calling Porzingis' absence indefinite. He will not travel with the team to Hawai'i, meaning he will miss at least the first four practices and the preseason opener against the LA Clippers next Sunday in Honolulu.

"I'm not marking him down as being out to start the season or anything like that," Dunleavy said. "He's just not available this week."

This has been a recurring issue for Porzingis, who has missed a combined 90 games the last two regular seasons primarily because of a mysterious health problem that emerged after he experienced a prolonged upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics in late February 2025.

Porzingis missed 10 of his first 11 games with the Warriors after they acquired him from the Atlanta Hawks at last February's deadline but did then return and appear in 16 of the final 21 games.

That, in part, motivated the Warriors to bring Porzingis back this summer on a two-year, $40 million deal, guaranteeing only $3 million in the second season to maintain flexibility next summer.

There was internal optimism about how Porzingis looked this summer. He was in the team's San Francisco facility and on the court in the last week and appeared to be cleared for training camp before Dunleavy received a call Sunday night about Porzingis' latest health issue.

"He's been participating in everything," Dunleavy said. "It just kind of popped up."

The Warriors are already without starting wings Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody to enter the season. Both are in the middle stages of extended rehab for serious knee injuries.

"We feel comfortable with everything [about Porzingis' status]," Dunleavy said. "Disappointed that he won't be out there [when training camp starts Tuesday], but it's early, so don't want to overreact to anything."
